title: Index a workpiece one of 7 equal divisions on a dividing head
instruction: Index the workpiece on the dividing head exactly one of 7 equal divisions (one seventh of a turn). One full turn of the index crank turns the workpiece one fortieth of a turn. The index plate has two hole circles: 20 holes on the inner circle and 21 holes on the outer circle, with hole 0 of each on the red zero line. The plunger pin is now in hole 0 of the 20-hole circle. Pull the yellow knob up to free the crank, set the plunger on the hole circle that gives an exact division, turn the crank the right number of whole turns and holes (either direction), let the pin drop into that hole, then let go of the knob and move the gripper away.
context: Before cutting gear teeth, spline grooves or bolt-hole patterns, a machinist indexes the workpiece on a dividing head. US Army Ordnance subcourse OD1644, Milling Machine Operations (armyordnance.tpub.com/od16448/od164480028.htm, 029 and 031): "Since there are 40 teeth in the worm wheel, one turn of the index crank causes the worm wheel, and consequently the index head spindle to, make one-fortieth of a turn"; turns per division = "40 by the number of equal divisions desired"; the sector "indicates the next hole in which the pin is to be inserted and makes it unnecessary to count the holes". For 7 divisions: 40/7 = 5 5/7 = 5 15/21 turns, so the 21-hole circle. A wrong hole or circle leaves the divisions unequal and scraps the part. Done by: Machinists (O*NET 51-4041.00).
setup: Station table; x forward from the line between the arm bases, y left from their midpoint, heights above the table top. Dividing head: dark-blue steel housing 15 x 31 cm, 5 cm tall (x 20.5 to 35.5 cm, y -6.5 to +24.8 cm), fixed by two dark steel clamp blocks (3 x 4 x 1.5 cm) at x 19 and 37 cm, y 9 cm. Index plate: grey steel disc 14 cm across, face 6.1 cm high, centre (28, 17) cm, fixed; inner circle 20 holes at 42 mm radius, outer circle 21 holes at 56 mm radius; each hole a 7 mm square pocket 5 mm deep; hole 0 of each circle red, both on a red zero line pointing forward (+x). Index crank: orange arm 18 mm wide, 7 cm high, turning about the plate centre. Plunger: slides along the arm between the two circles (a light spring pulls it inward, 0.4-1.0 N); 6 mm steel pin 4 mm deep in its hole, spring-loaded down (1.5 N seated, 2.6 N lifted 7 mm); yellow knob 20 mm across, 36 mm tall, bottom 8 cm high, spinning on the pin. Start: pin in hole 0 of the 20-hole circle. Workpiece: aluminium disc 100 mm across, 16 mm thick, top 7.8 cm high, centre (28, 0) cm; a red line from its centre to its rim points forward (+x) at a fixed green pointer. Both grippers open at the ready pose. One fixed layout.
scoring: Rest state: the pin down in a hole (its bottom at least 2.5 mm below the plate face), both grippers at least 80% open with their tool points at least 5 cm from the knob, the crank under 1 degree/s. The pin is on a circle when its centre is within 1.5 mm of that circle's radius. Spindle angle: the workpiece's rotation from its start, either direction. A tier counts (best so far) only after a rest state holds for 1 s. 1.0, success, the trial ends: pin in the 21-hole circle and spindle within 0.2 degrees of 360/7 = 51.43 degrees (5 turns + 15 holes; one hole is 0.43 degrees). 0.5: 21-hole circle and 5 whole turns (spindle 44.8 to 53.8 degrees), wrong hole. 0.25: 5 whole turns on the 20-hole circle. 0: fewer or more than 5 whole turns, whatever the circle, including the workpiece unmoved. 0, latched: the crank turned more than 3 degrees with the pin in a hole (forced), or a non-finite state.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. To reset: lift the pin, return the plunger to hole 0 of the 20-hole circle on the red zero line (the crank arm on the zero line), and turn the workpiece back so its red line points at the green pointer (on a real head, turn the crank backward 5 15/21 turns, or loosen the spindle lock). In simulation every part's start pose is rewritten and the joints re-enabled after each reset.
fidelity: No worm or wheel: each step the spindle is set to the crank's rotation / 40 in code, one way, so it cannot be back-driven. Plate and workpiece both face up for the overhead camera; a real head has the crank at right angles to the spindle. Holes are 7 mm square pockets for a 6 mm pin. A spring and slide stand in for the plunger's radial clamp. Crank arm, hub and slide are visual only: the crank turns through the knob. No backlash (either direction counts), no sector arms. Rigid shapes.
